'''Bin Liu''' is a chemist who is Professor and Provost's Chair at the [[National University of Singapore]]. Her research considers polymer chemistry and organic functional materials. She was appointed Vice President of Research and Technology in 2019. She was awarded the 2021 [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] Centenary Prize. She was the Senior Vice Provost (Faculty & Institutional Development) from 2022 to 2023. Currently, she is the Deputy President of Research and Technology.

== Early life and education ==
Liu was encouraged to study science by her parents.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Troeger|first=Anna|date=2021-01-21|title=Bin Liu: "Turn whatever you are dreaming about into reality"|url=https://www.advancedsciencenews.com/bin-liu-turn-whatever-you-are-dreaming-about-into-reality/|access-date=2021-06-12|website=Advanced Science News|language=en-US}}</ref> She was trained in organic chemistry at [[Nanjing University]], before moving to the [[National University of Singapore]] for graduate studies. Her doctoral research involved water-soluble conjugated polymers for organic electronic devices.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2019-05-29|title=Meet the 2019 ACS Nano Award Lecture Laureates|url=https://axial.acs.org/2019/05/29/2019-acs-nano-award/|access-date=2021-06-12|website=ACS Axial|language=en-US}}</ref> At first, she struggled to successfully synthesise polymers, but she mastered it after one year.<ref name=":0" /> She eventually moved to the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], where she worked as a postdoctoral researcher on the development and application of conjugated [[polyelectrolyte]] nanoparticles for biomedicine.<ref name=":1" /> In 2005 she returned to [[Singapore]] to start her professorship at the [[National University of Singapore]].{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

== Research and career ==
Liu is a professor at the [[National University of Singapore]]. Her early work considered novel materials for high efficiency solar cells. In particular, she focused on the design of hole transport materials and interpenetrating organic/inorganic networks.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=L'Oréal Singapore honours two distinguished women scientists|url=https://www.nas.gov.sg/archivesonline/data/pdfdoc/20110902002/l%27oreal_for_women_in_science_-_press_release.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200321080127/https://www.nas.gov.sg/archivesonline/data/pdfdoc/20110902002/l%27oreal_for_women_in_science_-_press_release.pdf |archive-date=2020-03-21 }}</ref> To ensure compatibility with multi-layer device fabrication protocols, Liu concentrated on the design of materials that are soluble in water and alcohols.<ref name=":0" /> In 2011, she started working on biocompatible luminogens which demonstrate [[aggregation-induced emission]].<ref name=":1" /> Such materials are non-emissive as dilute solutions but can assemble into intensely emissive aggregates.<ref>{{Cite web|title=President's Technology Award 2016|url=https://astarapp.a-star.edu.sg/psta/All%20Citations/2016/PTA%202016%20citation%20-%20Prof%20Liu%20Bin.pdf|access-date=2021-06-12}}</ref> They can serve as highly sensitive light-up molecular probes, which allow for the non-invasive tracking of analytes and biological processes in real-time.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|last=hermes|date=2016-01-15|title=20 of world's top researchers from Singapore|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/20-of-worlds-top-researchers-from-singapore|access-date=2021-06-12|website=The Straits Times|language=en}}</ref> In 2014 she formed a spin-out company, Luminicell, which commercialises this technology.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home Main Page|url=http://www.luminicell.com/|access-date=2021-06-12|website=Luminicell: Next Generation Trackers for Long-Term Cell Imaging|language=en-US}}</ref>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Liu moved her laboratory-based work online.<ref name=":0" /> She made use of [[machine learning]] to accelerate materials design. The algorithms created by Liu can predict the properties of particular molecular structures, and had screened several million molecules by the end of 2020.<ref name=":0" /> The machine learning models can evaluate structure-property relationships, allowing for the prediction of optical and electronic properties.<ref name=":0" />

Liu was awarded the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] [[Centenary Prize]] in recognition of her work in organic materials and nanomaterials.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Professor Bin Liu {{!}} 2021 Centenary Prize winner|url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/2021-winners/professor-bin-liu/|access-date=2021-06-12|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-GB}}</ref>
